mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate future rate hikes, causing a short-term discounting effect that depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar pre-hike regimes are not statistically lower than post-hike baselines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in FEDFUNDS for two consecutive months signals a shift to accommodative policy, which lowers real discount rates and increases expected equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: IC for this regime is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or 20-day forward returns are not higher than in neutral regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 fails over a 6-month window or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than in neutral labor regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, coinciding with a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), suggests robust supply-side momentum outweighing inflationary pressures, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 12-month MA while CPIAUCSL decreases over the next quarter
regime_hint: robust supply expansion with cooling inflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar demand-supply regimes are not superior (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) for three months, despite steady GDP demand proxies (GDPC1), signals supply-side easing that lowers cost pressures and supports corporate pricing power, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months while GDPC1 remains stable
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than in neutral supply regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings reported by HOUST accompanied by a sharp increase in monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) suggests wage inflation and labor market tightness, which elevates earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in a single month while PAYEMS rises over the same period
failure_condition: 20-day returns in similar labor-tightness episodes are not higher (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer credit availability (measured indirectly by the inverse of FEDFUNDS stance, here proxying via FEDFUNDS decline) coincides with a decline in retail sales proxies (not available in evidence catalog; fallback: use HOUST as proxy for consumer activity) over the next month, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days due to risk-off sentiment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines by >0.5pp while HOUST falls over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than in risk-on regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of declining consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) without a corresponding decline in industrial production (INDPRO), the market anticipates continued monetary easing, which lowers real rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days in any regime.
failure_condition: IC for this pattern is not significant across multiple macro regimes (p > 0.05).
